questions.prompt: Your `AppDbContext` has a `private string _currentUser` field set per request, and you register it with `AddDbContextPool`. What can go wrong?
options: Nothing; EF Core clears all fields before reuse
The app fails to start because pooled contexts can't have fields
`_currentUser` may still hold a previous request's value when the context is reused
Every request gets a brand-new context, so the field is always empty
questions.explanation: Pooling reuses `DbContext` instances. EF Core resets tracked entities and options, but not your custom state, which is why pooling requires the context to be stateless.

source.section: ⚠️ Example of What Not to Do with Pooling

questions.prompt: In `EnableRetryOnFailure(5, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10), null)`, what do `TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10)` and `null` mean?
options: Wait exactly 10 seconds before the first retry; `null` disables retries for deadlocks
The maximum delay between retries; `null` means use the default set of transient errors
The command timeout; `null` means no retry limit
The total time allowed for all retries; `null` means retry every error
questions.explanation: `5` is the maximum number of retries, the `TimeSpan` is the maximum delay between retries, and `null` keeps the default list of transient error numbers.

questions.prompt: The context is configured with `UseQueryTrackingBehavior(QueryTrackingBehavior.NoTracking)`. An endpoint needs to load an entity and update it. What does the lesson say to do?
options: Override it for that query with `.AsTracking()`
Switch the whole app back to tracking
Call `EnableSensitiveDataLogging(true)`
Nothing; NoTracking entities are saved automatically
questions.explanation: NoTracking is faster and lighter for read-heavy GET endpoints. When you need to update entities, you override it with `.AsTracking()`.

questions.prompt: An API maps a DTO into `new Project { Id = dto.Id, Name = dto.Name }`. Why set `_context.Entry(project).State = EntityState.Modified` before saving?
options: It is required for every update, even on tracked entities
It makes EF insert the entity as a new row
It reloads the entity's values from the database
EF isn't tracking this detached object, so marking it Modified tells EF to update all its columns
questions.explanation: A tracked entity loaded with `FindAsync` already knows what changed. A detached object from an API request doesn't, so `Modified` tells EF to treat it as updated.

questions.prompt: Put the concurrency conflict and merge-retry sequence in order.
steps: EF tries the UPDATE using the old `RowVersion`
The database rejects it and EF throws `DbUpdateConcurrencyException`
Merge the database values with the client's changes
Retry `SaveChangesAsync`, which now compares against the new `RowVersion`
questions.explanation: After merging, EF's original snapshot must be refreshed to the latest database values, or the retry compares against the stale version again.

source.section: That line is central to how EF Core handles concurrency retries

questions.prompt: In the retry loop, what happens if you merge the values but skip `entry.OriginalValues.SetValues(databaseValues)`?
options: The retry succeeds, but the merge is lost
The retry throws the same `DbUpdateConcurrencyException` again, because EF still holds the stale original `RowVersion`
EF deletes the row and inserts a new one
EF ignores the concurrency token from then on
questions.explanation: Loaded with `RowVersion = 10`, the row is now at 11. Until the snapshot is updated to 11, every retry compares against 10 and fails.
